name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,322

entries.clue: Language read externally in two universities (4)

indicators.note: 'externally' means on the outside, so only the outside letters of 'read' are kept
'in' places the pair of letters inside the two universities

annotation.surface: A student reading a language course that spans two universities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Read' looks like a verb about studying; here it only donates its first and last letters to sit between the two Us.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain name-by-category: the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in northern India.

blocks.note: an upper is a stimulant drug, cocaine being one example
drugs are 'cut' when mixed with cheaper substances

annotation.surface: A question about whether a line of blow was cocaine that had been adulterated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blow' is slang for cocaine, so the surface reads as drug talk; as the definition it is a punch. 'Perhaps' marks cocaine as just one example of an upper.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a boxer's rising punch to the chin is one kind of blow.

indicators.note: Romeo 'appears in' the other word, so R is placed inside it

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Shakespeare's Romeo turning up in a daft comedy skit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a comic sketch featuring Romeo; 'sketch' is really a rough first version.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an artist's rough preliminary drawing and a writer's first version share the sense.

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order

annotation.surface: A reformed criminal whose life was spared.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reformed criminal' reads as one phrase, an ex-offender; split it, and 'Reformed' is the definition while 'criminal' tells you to rearrange HE SPARED.
annotation.definitionFit: Taken literally, re-formed means formed again, given a new shape.

indicators.note: 'shot' in the slang sense of ruined or worn out, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A film being broadcast with one shot edited out.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface belongs to film-making, so 'shot' reads as a camera take; it actually means wrecked, telling you to rearrange the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the 1983 Michael Caine and Julie Walters picture, adapted from Willy Russell's play.

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so the phrase includes the answer within its letters

blocks.note: the run starts at the last letter of 'Such' and ends three letters into 'descent'

annotation.surface: Wondering what sort of descent leads down into the underworld.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a question about a journey into the underworld, which suits the answer perfectly; the answer is sitting in plain sight across the first three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name used as a synonym: the Greek realm of the dead.

entries.clue: Pictures thus framing a Cubist pioneer (7)

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so the first word goes around the A

annotation.surface: Pictures in frames on show, belonging to an early Cubist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Framing' fits the gallery surface so well it is easy to miss that it is the instruction, and the painter's name is itself the right answer for the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Spanish painter co-founded Cubism with Georges Braque.

blocks.note: hidden, obscure, as in a secret kept in the shadows
a brunette has brown or black hair

annotation.surface: A mysterious dark-haired woman.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as one description, the classic mysterious brunette; each defines the answer on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one adjective: secretive or obscure, and of hair, brown or black.

blocks.note: the verb, as in putting forward a resignation or a bid

annotation.walkthrough: 'Kind offer' reads as one phrase, a generous proposal; it is two definitions side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective meaning gentle and loving, and a verb meaning to present formally.

entries.clue: Level area to coat with metal: gold (7)

blocks.note: to plate = to coat with a thin layer of metal
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: Instructions from a workshop: coat the level surface in gold.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a gilding instruction; 'Level area' is really a geographical feature, a flat stretch of high ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain geographical synonym: a tableland, high ground that is flat on top.

indicators.note: to return is to turn back, so 'red' is written backwards
to box is to enclose, so the reversed word encloses CO

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned back

annotation.surface: A firm sending back red boxes as unwanted stock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returned' seems to belong to the firm sending goods back; it applies only to 'red', which then boxes the firm.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre usage: the design and furnishing of a stage set.

blocks.note: ed. = editor, the boss of a newspaper

annotation.surface: A newspaper editor who admired someone contemptible.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the editor did the admiring; in fact the two pieces simply sit side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: to rate someone is to think highly of them.

indicators.note: 'at first' points to the opening letter of 'solicitor'

annotation.surface: A courtroom where the judge makes fools of the solicitor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judge' reads as a noun, the person on the bench; as the definition it is the verb, to evaluate. A solicitor is a British lawyer who prepares cases.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to weigh up and form an opinion of something.

entries.clue: An emu three daughters trained for rider (8)

indicators.note: an animal that is trained is drilled into new habits, so the letters are drilled into a new order

annotation.surface: Three daughters taming an emu for someone to ride.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rider' sits in the animal picture as someone on the emu's back; it is actually a clause added to a document.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal usage: a rider is a clause tacked onto a bill or contract, an addition at the end.

entries.clue: Drama, initially unfolding in Mold, worked out (5,4,4)

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so take the first letter of 'unfolding'
'worked out' as in sorted and rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: A play first staged in the Welsh town of Mold and worked out there.
annotation.walkthrough: Mold is a town in north Wales, which makes the surface plausible for Dylan Thomas's Welsh play. 'Worked' looks like part of the story but joins the fodder, with 'out' as the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Dylan Thomas's 'play for voices' about a Welsh fishing village.

entries.clue: One imagines deer and ram cavorting (7)

definitions.note: 'One imagines' stands for 'one who imagines', a noun

indicators.note: to cavort is to leap about, so the letters jump into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone picturing a deer and a ram frolicking together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One imagines' reads as a throwaway 'I suppose'; it is the definition, a person who imagines.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun formed from the verb: someone given to fancies and visions.

entries.clue: Goalie who’s unlikely to be transferred? (6)

blocks.note: someone so good you would never let them go

annotation.surface: A goalkeeper so good the club will never sell him.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half reads as football transfer talk; it describes someone worth holding on to, the informal sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the short form of goalkeeper, and informal praise for a person worth not letting go.

indicators.note: what is heard is sound, so the word is taken by how it sounds

blocks.note: to dog = to trouble, to plague

annotation.surface: A court scene: a witness heard, trouble with a pirate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heard' looks like it goes with the witness giving evidence in court; it applies only to 'witness'.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: an old sailor, and in the Elizabethan sense a privateer or pirate.

entries.clue: Hamlet perhaps round clubs for disco (5)

indicators.note: 'round' means surrounding, so the Dane goes around the C

blocks.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, a Dane

annotation.surface: Hamlet going round the nightclubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' could be a small village; 'perhaps' shows he is one example of a Dane.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a disco is a party for dancing.

entries.clue: No lead on dog hunting bird (5)

indicators.note: the lead is the leading letter, and 'no lead' removes it

blocks.note: a beagle is a hunting dog

annotation.surface: A hunting dog off the leash chasing a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No lead' reads as a dog off its leash; the lead is really the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a large bird of prey.

annotation.surface: Fitting windows in a grand sitting room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' reads as a room, the natural place for windows; it is the verb, to laze about.
annotation.definitionFit: The glazier's trade verb: to fill window frames with glass.

annotation.surface: A fine cut from a script that fails badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine cut' reads as a delicate trim; each word is its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym, used of shows and films that bomb completely.

entries.clue: Fruit Mike brought into Spanish city (5)

indicators.note: Mike is 'brought into' the city, so M goes inside it

blocks.note: León, a city in northern Spain
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A man called Mike importing fruit into a Spanish city.
annotation.walkthrough: Mike looks like a trader; he is just the NATO code word for a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a sour yellow citrus.

blocks.note: to land someone with something = to burden them

annotation.surface: Resentment at the weight a nation has to carry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burden' is the tricky piece: you can be landed with a chore.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the island nation west of Great Britain.

indicators.note: food going off turns bad, so the letters spoil out of their order

annotation.surface: Cheese stored beside tinned meat, turning bad.
annotation.walkthrough: The fridge picture makes 'going off' read as spoiling food, which is exactly how it works as an indicator. Spam is a brand of tinned meat.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the hard Italian grating cheese from Parma.

annotation.surface: A man called Ray and his big grin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ray’s' reads as a man's name with a possessive; it is a shaft of light, and the ’s is just a join.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a shaft of light, and by extension a radiant smile.
